message.content:
Choosing “the best” movie of 2020 really comes down to what you’re looking for—critical acclaim, box‑office success, cultural impact, or personal taste—but here’s a quick snapshot of the most celebrated films released that year:

| Film | Director(s) | Why It Stands Out |
|------|-------------|-------------------|
| **“Parasite”** (re‑release) | Bong Joon‑ho | Won Best Picture at the 92nd Academy Awards (awarded in early 2021). Its sharp social satire and genre blending made it a global phenomenon even though its theatrical run began in late 2019. |
| **“Nomadland”** | Chloé Zhao | Winner of Best Picture & Best Actress (Frances McDormand) at the 93rd Oscars. A quiet meditation on modern American nomads that resonated deeply during lockdowns. |
| **“Soul”** | Pete Docter, Kemp Powers | Pixar’s Oscar‑winning animated feature earned praise for its philosophical depth and musical score. |
| **“1917”** | Sam Mendes | Technical marvel – one continuous shot illusion – plus intense war storytelling. |
| **“Joker”** | Todd Phillips | Dark psychological thriller that sparked debate over its portrayal of mental illness while topping worldwide grosses. |
| **“Tenet”** | Christopher Nolan | High‑concept sci‑fi action that pushed the limits of practical effects amid COVID restrictions. |

### How Critics Ranked Them  
* *Sight & Sound*’s end‑of‑year poll had **“Parasite,” “Mank,”** and **“Minari.”**  
* Rotten Tomatoes’ Top 10 listed **“Parasite,” “Jojo Rabbit,”** and **“Roma.”**

### Box Office Highlights  
Despite theater closures, several films performed strongly through streaming deals:
* **“Wonder Woman 1984”** (Warner Bros.) – $86 million domestic gross before moving online.  
* **“Bad Boys for Life”** (Sony Pictures) – $70+ million domestically despite limited release.

---

#### Bottom Line  
If you’re after critical consensus, **“Parasite”** remains the standout because of its historic Oscar win and universal themes. For heartfelt indie drama, **“Nomadland”** offers profound insight into contemporary America. And if you prefer animation, **“Soul”** delivers both emotional resonance and technical brilliance.

Feel free to let me know your preferred genre or style—I’d love to narrow it further!
